header:
Date: 2026-11-05T15:00:00Z
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Hill (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (EdgeBurst PM), Omar Martinez (EdgeBurst ML Eng), Diego Sun (EdgeBurst Infra)
Purpose: weekly POC standup to review TTFT and streaming performance, decide kernel path and next steps.
summary: Recap of last week's streaming handshakes and early token variability
Agreement to run targeted microburst traces and evaluate hedging vs priority queueing
Redwood to deliver kernel recommendation doc + security runbook
transcript:
[00:00] Lena: okay, starting, hello everyone, thanks for joining our weekly standup. um we've got 38 minutes. Marcus and I will cover the metrics then hand off to you for infra constraints.
[00:22] Priya: hey thanks, quick note, we've got a double booking later so we might have to drop at the 30 minute mark, but we'll try to stay through.
[00:40] Marcus: cool, I'll share my screen after the quick numbers — last run we saw median TTFT at 110 ms, p95 around 420, microburst tails spiking to 900ms under burst xfer. some of that looks like handshake serialization during streaming.
[01:05] Omar: yeah that aligns with what we saw in our traces — a bunch of 1s seqlen requests and then a few big 8k tokens ones, so the runtime's switching kernel and we hit a cold kv cache on the bigger requests.
[01:28] Lena: right, so two levers we discussed: aggressive prefix kv caching and a hedged early-response path for short queries. Marcus, what did the stream handshake tweak change?
[01:46] Marcus: i flipped the continuous batching threshold to 6ms and lowered the stream handshake timeout to 10ms, that trimmed median TTFT to 95ms in synthetic but p95 still high on real traffic — looks like kernel switching is the culprit.
[02:10] Diego: to add, on our side the infra is using mixed-instance pools — some V100s and a couple of T4 equivalents for cost — so kernel selection differs. we prefer not to change hardware mid-poc.
[02:33] Priya: can you explain kernel selection? our team thought that's a binary choice.
[02:42] Marcus: yeah fair — kernel's chosen by sequence length and model size, but runtime also factors in available memory and quantization path. with mixed GPUs you get different optimized kernels; that causes the runtime to recompile or pick a slower path for certain sequences.
[03:05] Priya: okay that explains the spikes.
[03:10] Marcus: and another nuance: streaming handshake can add 40-80ms if the first chunk waits for a large kernel to be ready.
[03:23] Omar: hmm, so for us where 70% are sub-512 tokens, we should prioritize a fast small-kernel path and hedging for bigger ones?
[03:35] Marcus: exactly. one approach: keep a fast small-kernel primed in standby and route short seqlen to it; for long ones either accept slower path or run async fallback.
[03:46] Lena: cost tradeoff though — priming standby kernels increases memory footrpint and unit cost.
[03:52] Priya: what kind of cost delta are we talking?
[03:56] Marcus: rough numbers: keeping an extra primed kernel raises GPU memory usage ~12-18% and per-token cost roughly 5-7% in our bench. but it reduces TTFT p50 by 30-40ms.
[04:15] Diego: budget matters. EdgeBurst wants predictable cost for production. we can't overspend.
[04:23] Lena: good, so decision matrix: prioritize TTFT for <512 tokens; evaluate priming cost vs hedged fallback. Diego, can you share constraints?
[04:33] Diego: we have a hard limit of +10% on infra changeable costs during pilot. we can reallocate within pool but not increase spend.
[04:42] Marcus: ok we can simulate priming by running a small number of warmup sequences during low traffic to mimic standby kernels without incurring full-time cost — cheap experiment.
[04:56] Priya: that sounds promising.
[05:02] Marcus: also ran a quantization pass — 4-bit symmetric — didn't change TTFT much but improved throughput. some devs saw minor hallucination in outputs but for our use case it's acceptable.
[05:20] Omar: did you test KV cache warmup? we saw cold cache penalties of 150-220ms on long requests.
[05:28] Marcus: yes, kv cache prefetch reduced those cold misses by half in synthetic. but real traffic patterns have bursts that evict the cache.
[05:40] Lena: if bursts are evicting cache, we should look at smarter eviction policies or sharded caches.
[05:48] Diego: sharding is possible but adds complexity to our infra changes.
[05:53] Priya: what about batching? can we batch more aggressively without hurting latency?
[05:58] Marcus: continuous batching helps but only if sequences align; microbursts make batching variable. priority queueing that lumps short queries could help.
[06:13] Lena: let's list the experiments for next week. Marcus?
[06:18] Marcus: one: microburst replay with 10k traces under current pool (seqlen bins 1-256,257-1024,>1024). two: warm-priming experiment during low-util windows. three: hedged early-response for <512 tokens. four: eviction policy tweak — lru -> freq-based for KV cache.
[06:40] Omar: i'll attach the real histograms after this call.
[06:44] Priya: Diego will confirm cost constraints.
[06:47] Diego: yes, i'll validate the +10% and confirm whether we can reassign GPUs.
[06:53] Lena: cool. quick security question — Priya asked about data residency and SOC2. Diego, any blockers?
[06:59] Diego: we need SAML SSO + audit log integration. we can host in our VPC but need KMS for keys.
[07:09] Lena: Redwood can share SOC2 excerpt and VPC runbook. i'll email it tonight.
[07:16] Priya: thanks.
[07:20] Marcus: small divergence — one of the microburst traces showed a repeatable 1.1s spike tied to disk swap on one node. that's infra-level, Diego, can we check node-level IO?
[07:35] Diego: oh that's likely a misconfigured swap or ephemeral disk throughput issue; i'll have infra look at node logs.
[07:45] Marcus: ok we'll mark that as infra action.
[07:49] Lena: any objections to the plan?
[07:52] Priya: none from product.
[07:55] Omar: sounds good.
[07:57] Lena: great. recap — Marcus runs microburst replay and priming sim; Omar provides histograms; Diego confirms cost and infra IO; Lena sends security and runbook.
[08:12] Priya: i'll book the Nov 17 benchmark slot for Diego and the Redwood team.
[08:19] Lena: perfect. thanks all. meeting adjourned.
